name: story
wording: One thin slice of behaviour a user can rely on, handed over by the architect in the design's own terms: the slice and why it is wanted, its acceptance criteria, what is out of scope, the path it takes, whether its changes ship, show or ask, its rough cost, and examples where misunderstanding is likely. It starts only when the operator signs off its read-back. It spans bounded contexts only where one architect holds them all; otherwise one story per context, joined by contracts. It is done when its acceptance criteria hold in the project's shared work; when it ends, merged or dropped, its examples leave with it unless the architect keeps them.
reason: The operator: the design state a session reads was long human prose restating facts across concepts and carrying decisions with their situations; its reader is a model, so the state is the design alone, each concept as its established name and residue, and decisions and their reasons are history. Restated as its established name and residue, standalone, each fact in the one concept it belongs to, with the meaning standing decisions carried folded in.
